thread:
maria: heads up — hit a weird race on a production node during the last canary. two shards claimed the same prefix and both served reads for ~3s before eviction caught up. logs attached below.

maria: logs (truncated):
```
2026-03-15T12:03:10Z CLAIM shard=shard-17 prefix=/user/  epoch=842
2026-03-15T12:03:10Z CLAIM shard=shard-21 prefix=/user/  epoch=842
2026-03-15T12:03:12Z READ shard=shard-17 prefix=/user/ req=tok_... ok
2026-03-15T12:03:12Z READ shard=shard-21 prefix=/user/ req=tok_... ok
2026-03-15T12:03:13Z EVICT shard=shard-17 prefix=/user/ reason=claim_conflict
```

maria: looks like both nodes observed the same epoch and proceeded to claim; eviction later resolved but we had stale-apparent-duplicate-reads. not catastrophic but violates our single-owner invariant for prefix writes (reads are OK but confusing for metrics).

chen: hmm. do we have the claim token unique per node? I thought we incremented epoch + holder-id.

devon: we do `epoch + holder-id` in the token, but the race is likely between the lease refresh path and the rebalancer commit. both sides think they won.

liam: can you paste the claim flow you hit? is this the same as the "claim then publish lease" race we saw last quarter?

maria: simplified sequence: requestor A and B concurrently see slot free -> both try Claim() with epoch 842 -> both write claim meta -> both start serving because they see a valid token -> later reconcile job sees last-writer and issues eviction to loser.

chen: classic last-writer-wins without fencing. options: 1) add a central sequencer; 2) make Claim() conditional CAS on epoch+counter; 3) introduce short fence window where only claimers with a cert get to serve.

devon: prefer minimal invasive change: attach a short Paxos-ish serial number to claims so Claim() returns success only to the winner. other callers get a failure; they wait and fetch new owner. avoids full central sequencer.

liam: tradeoffs: adding serialization increases latency on cold claim path — maybe 5-10ms per claim. But claim frequency is low for hot prefixes.

maria: we should also consider demote vs immediate hard-evict. right now eviction is a best-effort async job that can be slow. if we wait for eviction to complete before other node serves, we lose availability on failover.

chen: what if we switch to a two-phase handover: 1) outgoing node marks prefix DEMOTED (still serves reads for a short grace TTL but rejects writes); 2) incoming node obtains CLAIM while outgoing is in DEMOTED state; once incoming warms KV and confirms no active writers, it enters ACTIVE and outgoing transitions to EVICTED.

devon: that mirrors a lot of database handoffs. It keeps reads available, prevents write skew. Need to define semantics: DEMOTED should block write-paths at the runtime level (error code?) and surface to callers as 409 so clients can retry.

liam: implementation detail: DEMOTED marker must be replicated before accepting it as real. otherwise split-brain on network partitions. use our existing meta-log with sync quorum. that makes handover slower but safer.

maria: instrumentation we should add before changing: count of simultaneous-claim incidents, time-between-claim-and-evict, number-of-reads-during-conflict, write-failures-due-to-demote. call them `claim_conflict_count`, `claim_to_evict_ms`, `conflict_reads` and `demote_write_rejects`.

cachebot: automated note: created ticket INF-4321 for metrics + canary run plan. assignees needed.

chen: proposed experimental plan:
- short-term patch: make Claim() strictly CAS (server returns failure if not last-writer) + add metric `claim_retries`. deploy to canary.
- medium-term: implement two-phase DEMOTED handover semantics, wire write-path to return 409 during DEMOTED. run a 1% traffic canary.
- long-term: evaluate whether we need a sequencer for very hot rebalancing workloads (heatmap needed).

devon: for the CAS-only patch we should also add a fast-path backoff: if Claim() fails, caller polls owner meta for up to 200ms before retry; that should dampen thundering herd.

maria: action items:
- chen -> prototype CAS-only Claim() diff + metrics (due EOD 3/17)
- devon -> small bench to measure extra latency on cold-claim path (start 3/18)
- liam -> update runtime write-path error mapping so 409 from runtime surfaces as `PrefixDemoted` in SDK (due 3/24)
- maria -> run canary config once CAS patch lands and collect `conflict_reads` and `claim_retries`.

liam: question: do we need a migration for existing prefixes in metadata? probably just compatibility layer: old entries without DEMOTED flag treated as ACTIVE.

chen: sounds good. I'll open the PR early tomorrow, include logs and the new metric names.

maria: thanks. if we go with DEMOTED semantics, we should document escape-hatches for enterprise customers who can't tolerate write 409s (fallback policy to tolerate dual writes with compensation).

devon: note: consider adding a debug flag that makes Claim() verbose and emits trace-id in meta so we can follow a prefix claim lifecycle in production traces.

maria: agreed. adding `claim_trace_id` to meta would help replaying incidents.

liam: ok let's sync after PR is up. :thumbsup:

cachebot: incident-note: no customer impact reported. metrics spike observed 2026-03-15 12:03 UTC.

maria: thanks all — closing thread, will post the PR link in this channel when ready.
